_comment: One source for the hook list and what each model is for. Read by lib/jev.py and lib/models.py, and at runtime by the claude-loadout binary from the installed plugin.

hooks.bash_gate: asks before risky or outward shell commands
hooks.edit_gate: asks before a write git cannot undo
hooks.narrow: trims bulky output before it enters context
hooks.model_router: picks the model each subagent runs on
hooks.loop_detect: notices a tool call going nowhere
hooks.stop_check: stops unverified claims and empty promises
hooks.subagent_verify: checks a subagent's report against its work

criteria.opus: implementation: the task itself must change code in several files, or make failing tests or a build pass, iterating edit, run, fix, where a wrong step is expensive to unwind. TRUE: implement an issue, feature or plan node and open a PR; fix a bug and add a regression test; make failing tests pass; a multi-file refactor; an audit or sweep that must also FIX what it finds across several files. FALSE (not this): a READ-ONLY audit, review or investigation of code, even a deep, adversarial or security one, even one that says root-cause or find bugs; a one-line or config edit; a mechanical rename or find-and-replace, even across many files and followed by a build; rebuilding, deploying or running known commands; writing a report or docs.
criteria.fable: design: the deliverable is a plan, spec, ADR or design recommendation for how something SHOULD work, weighing tradeoffs. TRUE: write an implementation plan; write a spec, contract or ADR; recommend one design among options. FALSE (not this): auditing or reviewing existing code or changes for bugs or security holes, however deep or adversarial; summarising what exists; a findings or incident report; implementing a plan that is already written.
criteria.sonnet: investigation and mechanical work: read, search and audit code without fixing it, including read-only security audits, adversarial reviews and root-cause investigations; summarise what exists; run known commands, builds or deploy steps; edit config or one file; a mechanical rename or find-and-replace, even across many files; follow a procedure that is already decided; write a findings report or update docs. FALSE (not this): a task that must implement a change across files and iterate until tests pass; an audit or consistency pass that also changes the files it finds wrong; a single command or lookup.
criteria.haiku: a small lookup: run one given command and report its output, find a file, list values, extract a field, reformat something short; a handful of tool calls where a mistake is obvious and cheap. FALSE (not this): anything that needs reading several files or judging what they mean.

ranking._comment: Hooks in order of observed usefulness, best first. Loadout sorts its hooks page by this and shows each score. Scores: +2 clearly valuable, +1 useful, 0 mixed or neutral, -1 costs more than it returns, null not yet scorable. Re-rank as data accrues: read decisions.jsonl and the session transcripts, classify each firing helpful / false positive / neutral by what happened next, and update as_of and basis.
ranking.basis: decisions.jsonl 2026-09-19..22 (5,800 Jev calls), 41 session transcripts; mostly pre-version-stamp decisions, so current code has only 13-16 each

order.why: every reviewed ask was a write git could not undo
rare, sensible trims of bulky reads
caught prod rolls and merges; asks on most heredoc edits git could undo
real catches, but blocks questions and command blocks meant for the user
advisory only; model hints mostly ignored
